Avendus on India's Microfinance Sector

Over the next 5-6 years, we expect the industry to be driven by four secular themes:
i) tapping India's diverse geographic potential
ii) deeper rural market penetration
iii) rising engagement with new-to-credit (NTC) customers
iv) accelerated digital adoption.

These levers coupled with huge unmet demand are expected to propel gross loan portfolio (GLP) to grow at 15%+ CAGR, reaching INR 10 trillion over the next 5-6 years.

We believe the industry will return to its historical cross-cyclical ROEs of 20% over the next 5-6 years

Money Control on SJS Enterprises: Strong Q4 FY25, new products, clients growth drivers

One of the company’s key growth drivers is the rising demand for premium vehicles, including big cars, SUVs, and high-end bikes, now extending to the consumer durable segment.

As per the management, the content per vehicle is expected to rise 4-6x from the current level of Rs 3,500-5,000 per vehicle.

New clients offer significant opportunities

In Q1FY25, SJS on-boarded Dixon Technologies as a client. It operates in the consumer electronics, lighting, home appliances, and mobile phone segments.

SJS has already started small-scale supplies to Dixon, and the management has indicated a significant opportunity that could be a key growth lever for the next phase of growth.

In April 2025, the company on-boarded Hero Motocorp as its client to supply decal and logos for many models. The management indicated that HMCL sources these products worth Rs 250 crore annually, a significant part of which should flow to SJS.

Julius Bar on Union Budget 2025-2026 - Consumption Booster; Good summary of Sector related impact

The Budget, at a margin, has been a non-event from capital markets perspective

The economic activity levels slowed during 2024 due to elections disruptive rainfall. With these drags in the base and government spending supporting consumption, the earnings growth is set to improve to 12-13% in FY26E

Sectors with double-digit earnings growth include industrials, property, banks, two-wheelers, and telecoms.

Overall, we continue to remain constructive on the Indian equity markets, driven by earnings cycle and strong domestic liquidity, coupled with likely comeback of FPI flows. Markets could be volatile in H1CY25, as debates persist around Donald Trump policies and comeback of India’s earnings growth momentum. We would recommend to buy the potential ‘dips’.

MSCI November Rejig: Nuvama Sees Boost In HDFC Bank Weightage, Inclusion Of Adani Energy

The November round of rejig in MSCI indices may lead to a boost in HDFC Bank Ltd.'s weightage, according to Nuvama Alternative & Quantitative Research.

HDFC Bank could attract inflows amounting to $1.88 billion, Nuvama said in a report released on Tuesday, two days before the scheduled rejig of the MSCI indices. The private lender is included under the MSCI Global Standard Index.

As per Nuvama's forecast, Adani Energy Solutions Ltd., along with Kalyan Jewellers Ltd., Oberoi Realty Ltd., and Alkem Laboratories Ltd., could be added to the index. Among the probable additions is also BSE Ltd., one of the two main stock exchanges in India.

The official announcement on the adjustments in the MSCI indices is scheduled at 2:30 a.m. (IST) on Nov. 7. The rejig will come into effect on Nov. 25.

1) CHINA’S PAIN IS INDIA’S GAIN: 
With close to 1000GW and aided by 50%+ over capacity; China will continue to remain the world’s factory for modules, cells and other key technologies like ESS and Electrolysers. 

This essentially implies that module and cell prices will continue to remain benign maintaining stability for Indian module cos.

2) RATE OF CELL TECHNOLOGY CHANGES SHOULD DECLINE 

TopCon constitutes 75% of the Chinas cell capacity (750GW) which implies next 10-12 qtrs will see no meaningful tech change which is essential. Even though there are enough players who have moved or planning to move to HJT (40GW, hetero junction tech), adoption will be slow. Money Control on CMS Info Systems

New order win in the quarter was Rs 600 crore, taking the total order book to Rs 5,000 crore, offering good visibility. The management has reiterated its guidance of Rs 2,500-2,700 crore revenue by FY25, with a 60:40 split in the cash management and managed services businesses.

At the current market price (CMP), CMS Info Systems trades at an FY26 PE of 15.2 times and PEG of 0.88 times. The fair value, estimated using the DCF methodology, is higher than the current market price, and, therefore, indicates a good upside from here.

This has been one of our high-conviction stock ideas and has gained 43.2 percent in the last one year. We continue to remain overweight on the stock and recommend a ‘buy’.

Money Control on Indigo

In Q4 FY24, the company expanded its fleet by adding 9 aircraft, bringing the total to 367. The management has projected a 10-12 percent YoY increase in capacity in Q1 FY25 capacity, measured in ASKs. Its long-term vision is to double the size of IndiGo by the end of this decade, supported by an order for 500 aircraft, which should help achieve this goal.

IndiGo's valuation is at a reasonable level, with shares trading at 5.8 times the projected FY26 EV/EBITDAR. As market leader, the airline has the potential to grow its earnings at a faster pace. We recommend investors to accumulate the stock with a long-term perspective.

Money Control on IdeaForge Technology: Improving business a sign of possible stock rerating

The company has entered international markets and has seen a good traction in the US with few trials and other activities, which are expected to bring more business in the coming months.

The company is expecting good orders in the fiscal 2025, particularly from the US market where the focus will be on civil orders. At present, civil accounts for about 31% of its revenue and the company aims to take it to 40%, while the rest is coming from defence.

Order Book book is now around Rs 124.7 crore as against an annual revenue of Rs 314 crore, providing good visibility for growth. The company is having a L1 (lowest bidder) pipeline of over Rs 300 crore. Some of this could come in Q1FY25.

Company is expecting margins to be in the region of 25-30% in the coming quarters as against 17.5% EBITDA margins in the fiscal year 2024.

Money Control on Medi Assist - Strong business growth, but margin moderates; Synergies from acquisitions can improve margins over the next 3-4 quarters

Margins fell due to integration-related costs; Health insurance in sweet spot, TPAs have become indispensable

The company had net cash balance in the books of Rs 245 crore at the end FY24 even after the acquisitions done in the past 12-15 months. It delivered an ROE (return on equity) of 19 percent in FY24.

Medi Assist’s stock has risen 18 percent over its IPO price after its listing in Jan ’24. The company is trading at a valuation of 26 times estimated earnings for FY26, which is reasonable considering an ROE of 19% in FY24.

The valuation can re-rate given the annuity like revenues, high operating leverage, and dominant market position in a growing industry.

Given the sectoral tailwinds and Medi Assist’s vantage positioning, we expect the stock to be a long-term compounder.  Long-term investors should accumulate the stock in a staggered manner.

Sansera engineering

Future business outlook based on management commentary

Outlook: Sansera engineering is on track to exceed previous guidance for utilization rates and expects continued growth in FY25, with a focus on emerging segments. Sansera aims to achieve 40% revenue from emerging segments by FY27 and has a positive outlook for the defense segment. The company also aims to double EV revenue in FY25. Capex for FY24 stood at Rs.3.4 billion, with expectations of lower capex in FY25. Sansera is confident in managing debt through cash flow generation and has improved its debt-to-equity ratio in FY24. However, concerns include potential delays in aerospace orders and margin improvement in the Sweden facility. The company is actively seeking opportunities to invest in advanced startups and transitioning to a subsystem supplier for international OEMs.

Credits: ScoutQuest via Twitter

Endurance Technologies

Future business outlook based on management commentary

Outlook: Endurance Technologies is focused on shifting its product mix towards higher-margin segments and expanding into the 4W and non-automotive sectors. They aim to increase the share of 4W business in consolidated revenue from 6.5% to 45% by FY30. The company remains committed to the EV space and aims to reach 10% of India sales in the aftermarket business by FY28. Endurance is actively pursuing M&A opportunities in Europe and is optimistic about its future growth prospects, despite concerns about the slowdown in EV orders and uncertainty in the European automotive market. The company is also working on reducing its environmental impact and achieving carbon neutrality in its plants.

Credits: ScoutQuest via Twitter

Solar Industries

Future business outlook based on management commentary

Outlook: Solar Industries Management is Aiming for 30% topline growth in FY25. Expecting 15% volume growth in domestic explosives business. Expecting threefold growth in defense revenue in FY25, reaching around 20% of total revenue. Rs.800 crore planned for FY25, allocated to defense and explosives businesses. Expecting further improvement in EBITDA margins. Record high defense order book at Rs.2600 crore, with expectations of significant future orders. Expanding into the Rajasthan market and Saudi Arabia.

Money Control on Intellect Design Arena Outlook & Valuation

The management commentary indicates a large pipeline and advanced discussion on new products. This should translate into strong growth in the medium term. The GeM contract loss, while hitting the top line, released resources that are to be channelled to new products that cater to domestic and overseas markets. The company is already in discussions with some of the state governments for a licensing deal. 

The next 12-18 months are crucial for the company with deal conversion and favourable operating leverage playing out, and earnings growth is expected to pick up. Weak tech spending in the BFSI sector appears to be bottoming out and, therefore, the recovery phase should see higher deal flows, benefitting Intellect Design.

Valuation 

At the CMP, Intellect Design trades at an FY26 PE of 24x and a PEG of 0.7x,  which in our view indicates a good upside potential. We retain our overweight rating and recommend investors to buy the stock.

Money Control on Polycab Outlook & Valuation

As the country experiences an infrastructure up-cycle, Polycab will continue to be on a growth path. However, its market capitalisation has more than trebled in the past three years. The stock is now trading at an elevated valuation of 42x on FY26 earnings, leaving limited room for further rerating. More importantly, investors should be watchful of the outcome of the tax evasion investigation by the IT department as it could add volatility to the stock.

Money Control on BSE

What will be the impact on profitability ?

The BSE will have to make a one-time provisioning for all the past dues (till end FY24) which would be around Rs 164 crore. However, these regulatory charges will be recurring cost and will be higher in the future as BSE’s notional turnover in equity derivatives is rising. The future impact is a bigger concern as it will lead to the downgrading of future earnings and will limit the stock upside.

BSE might take a price hike

In all likelihood, the BSE may increase prices on equity derivatives to mitigate the impact of higher regulatory cost. 

What should investors do?

At the current market price, the BSE stock is trading at 44 times estimated core earnings for FY26. Investors shouldn’t exit in a jiffy as there is high chances of price hikes. Some clarity may emerge after the FY24 earnings are announced on May 8.

Money Control on KPIT

Outlook 

KPIT has retained a dominant position in the auto ERD space and has been delivering a strong double-digit YoY growth, quarter after quarter. Large deal win flow from Diamond & Platinum accounts hasn’t stopped and the company’s ramp-up is driving growth. Global automotive OEMs are investing to make rapid progress towards SDV and new fuel technologies. KPIT has been focused on its core practices, including SDV, middleware, and electrification, and aims to expand towards the adjacencies as well as new markets, including China & India, to sustain growth.

FY25 guidance of 18-22 percent CC revenue growth is likely conservative. EBIT margin guidance of 20.5 percent includes the impact of Rs 100 crore ESOP costs for FY25.

Valuation 

At the CMP of Rs 1,508.5, KPIT trades at an FY26 PE of 43 times and a PEG of 1.6x, which is the lowest among peers, including LTTS, Tata Elxsi and Tata Technologies. Investors may add the stock on dips to build a position in the stock.

Real Estate Sales are awesome, so, what's next!?

Last two years, avg real estate sales across different micro markets is about 30-50% higher than pre-covid. 

As these sales start turning into construction over the next 24-48 months, we should see strong demand for building material products.

Goldman Sachs like Pipes in this category because pipes are low cost and high critical item.

% of total material cost:
Pipes: ~3%
Tiles: ~7%
Wires: 4-5%
Cement: 16-18%
Paints:~6%

Replacement cost is high (you have to break the flooring and walls for any repairs) and that makes them critical.

Additionally, pipes are a must BUY whereas some of the other materials have direct dependency on occupancy timelines, the purpose (investment versus personal use) etc...

Goldman Sachs likes Astral and Prince Pipes

Money Control on ION Exchange: Stock offers better risk-reward ratio after recent correction

ION Exchange boasts of a healthy order book of Rs 3,303 crore, providing visibility for the next 2-3 years. Furthermore, the bid pipeline looks robust, with around Rs 8,526 crore.

ION Exchange is investing approximately Rs 400 crore in a new resin production facility at Roha. Commercial production is expected to begin in FY25-26, with full capacity utilisation anticipated within 3-4 years.

The company is also on track to achieve breakeven in EBIT in its consumer products division by FY23, signifying a promising new revenue stream. In Q3FY24, the segment achieved a strong 38% YoY growth in revenues, led by strong demand. On an overall basis, the company has guided a revenue growth of ~20% in FY2025

The stock now trades at a P/E ratio of 18x, based on fiscal 2026 estimates. This is attractive in the light of improving earnings visibility, backed by strong orders in hand and an equally robust pipeline of new projects

The fall started after the company posted a tepid performance in Q3FY24 and aggravated later amidst the meltdown in mid- and small-cap stocks. Following the price correction, Protean is now trading at an attractive valuation of 27 times FY25 estimated earnings.

Protean’s current top line is dominated mainly by three business lines – tax services, NPS and identity services (online PAN verification, e-KYC transactions, Aadhaar authentication, etc).

The company is diversifying from 3- 7 lines of business. It is evolving three more verticals – Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), data (account aggregator) and cloud and infosec services.

Protean is the only technology service provider which powers the entire network on which the ONDC ecosystem runs.

Nifty 50, or the benchmark index, is closer to the long-term average (10 years), followed by the Mid-cap index and then the small-cap index. The small-cap index trades at 31.52 per cent above the long-term average, while the mid-cap index is 24.65 percent above its 10-year average.

The primary concern lies within the small cap segment. The assets under management (AUM) of small and mid-cap funds managed by AMCs are nearing those of larger cap funds.

While the size of the various funds is nearly the same, the size of the market they are chasing is not. Large-cap stocks command 75 percent of the market cap, while mid-cap funds are 16 percent, and small-cap funds are just nine percent of the market cap of the Nifty 500 index.

Money Control Weekly Tactical Pick: Why this jewellery maker is set to glitter

SGL is tripling its production capacity from 270 kgs now to about 750-800 kgs per month and has shifted its production base to a larger plant at Navi Mumbai. SGL is also targeting to double the number of jewellery designs to 7,000 per month. The company is eyeing a top-line CAGR of  ~43% over the FY24-27 period

SGL will increase its share of wallet from existing domestic B2B consumers — leading jewellery retail chains such Malabar Gold & Diamonds, Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, and Senco Gold. 

SGL is in talks with leading national level jewellery retailers to initiate supplies, which will provide an additional growth trigger

SGL will now be able to access debt for working capital via gold metal loans. These loans will almost halve the interest cost to 5.5%, boosting earnings. We expect SGL earnings to grow at 60% CAGR over the FY24-26 period.

SGL promoters recently picked up a 1.5 percent stake in the company at Rs 1,017

Hindustan Aeronautics: Strong earnings visibility and order pipeline to support stock valuation

Monopoly status, advanced manufacturing capabilities, global partnerships, and a robust order book augur well for the company

With an order book close to Rs 82,000 crore, equivalent to three times its annual revenue, HAL is well positioned for sustained growth. Recent partnerships with industry giants such as GE and Airbus highlight the company's commitment to advanced defence programmes and achieving higher operational scale. The possibility of securing orders worth Rs 45,000 crore in the next 8-12 months is another positive for HAL. Additionally, the company is  aggressively looking to expand exports, which should support higher growth.

HAL's stock is now trading at 25 times i The strong order book and earnings visibility position HAL as an attractive investment opportunity.

Kirloskar Ferrous Industries: Capex completion, cost savings to support earnings growth

In the September 2023 quarter, one of the blast furnaces was shut down, leading to a reduction in the production of pig iron. All the three blast furnaces are operational and this should drive sales volumes in H2FY24

KFIL has acquired 100 percent equity in Oliver Engineering, based in Punjab, which is into the business of ferrous castings and machining with a capacity of 28,000 metric tonnes per annum.

KFIL can target customers based in north India. We expect the plant to be operational by March 2024.

ISMT will be investing Rs 100 crore in de-bottlenecking projects, which should be completed by June 2024 and help increase sales revenue.

KFIL has the highest market share of pig iron, and with all the backward integration projects in place, it will be in a much better position, compared to other players.

We remain positive on KFIL and investors with high-risk appetite can accumulate the stock.

Money Control on Paradeep Phosphates - Starting this fiscal, Paradeep Phosphates should see a lot of efficiencies kicking in from its backward integration investments. The management expects ~Rs 200 crore of additional annual EBITDA to be generated from all these initiatives. We think PPL has a solid footing to remain cost competitive and become a much larger player in the complex fertiliser space.

Money Control on NMDC - We have increased our projection for realisation and EBITDA per tonne for the rest of FY24 and FY25. Higher visibility on volumes, along with cost-saving projects, will aid earnings growth. A debt-free balance sheet and lower capex, compared to the free cash flows, should support higher dividend or buyback from NMDC, supporting valuation. We remain positive on NMDC and recommend high-risk investors to add and accumulate the stock on declines.

It's important to clarify that these charts do not serve as buy or sell recommendations. Instead, consider them an additional data point when tracking these companies.

In addition to these charts, it is crucial to monitor fundamental events, including earnings dates, key management personnel (KMP) resignations, government policy announcements, and so forth.

We promise to improvise the aesthetics of the charts going forward

Around a year ago, when I initially launched this channel, my objective was quite straightforward. I wanted to provide a platform for sharing research reports for those who were interested in studying various companies that I was discussing on Twitter. This initiative was born out of the limitation on Twitter, which did not support PDF attachments.

Over time, our scope expanded from merely sharing my own research to embracing a broader approach: "Let's share all the valuable reports we can find." As the channel grew, I also started posting daily updates.

In the recent past, the "I" in our endeavor transformed into a collective "WE" as more hands joined in. With this newfound collaboration, we began contemplating how we could provide even more value to our audience. Amid numerous ideas, to begin with, we've settled on one that truly excites us.

We are delighted to announce our latest offering: "The Techno Corner." This curated selection represents the best technical setups we've come across during our research.…

▪️ Within BFSI we continue to expect improved performance from NBFCs as a stable rate environment tends to cap their borrowing costs.

▪️ Benefits of easing inflationary pressure, reflected in the margins of autos and consumer companies on expected line.

▪️ We see this trend playing out in 2Q also but consumer companies may pass on benefits to compete effectively with regional players.

▪️ We remain cautious of erratic weather conditions and its impact on agri commodities, as it is capable of denting investor returns.

JM Financial Deep Dive on India Chemicals: Time to place the right bets amid the recent slowdown

We recommend two themes

a) acceleration of Europe+1 for fluorination players: Navin Fluorine and SRF are our structural top picks as we believe imminent HFC production cuts in the EU and the US will have a cascading benefit for India’s fluorine-based complex specialty chemicals players

b) continuation of basic chemicals’ import substitution: Lifetime-low phenol spreads and upcoming capacities for bisphenol-a and other basic chemicals make Deepak Nitrite a good BUY candidate.

Within our coverage, there are other differentiated plays such as Clean Science, Aether Industries, and Archean Chemicals where earnings recovery could occur in 2HFY24.

Jeffereis India Forum 2023 - Insights

Positive outlook from Cyclicals: Companies across cyclicals (property, cap-goods, cement, industrials) was broadly positive.

Property cos have seen strong start to FY24 residential pre-sales, and pricing strength is visible. Contracting capacity is in short supply.

Strong order-book trends with cap-goods cos are continuing; while industrials are seeing some margin tailwinds on declining energy and commodity prices. 

Cement cos are expecting healthy volume growth; even as pricing is flattish (though lower costs a tailwind).

Chemicals are expecting to >2x revenues over the next 3/4 years as capacity in China recedes.

Autos (PV, 2Ws) expressed reasonably good demand with good orderbooks (PVs) and margin trends stable to positive.

Zydus Lifesciences: Time to book profit, post strong rally over a year?

Zydus Lifesciences posted strong quarterly numbers in Q4FY23, led by Revlimid sales. This is yet another good quarterly show.

While this leaves FY23 with a high base, the management is aiming for a single-digit growth in the US market for FY24 on the back of launches from the Moraiya facility.

Domestic businesses remain steady on the back of oncology and consumer brands. Going forward, the key watch would be the progress in the NCE (New Chemical Entity) portfolio, for which incremental R&D spending is allocated.

Having said that, given the expectation of a moderation in top-line growth and post the strong rally over the year, valuations are close to the fair level.

HUL is finding it difficult to get off the inflation tiger

Lower prices are not seeing growth bounce back. One explanation is that it’s a really weak demand environment. But HUL may also be partly to blame 

There could be another hurdle in HUL’s path to higher growth -- its unwillingness to let margins drop below a certain level. If competition is willing to do that then it could lead to share erosion too. In HUL’s categories of home care and foods & refreshment, its segment margin in the March quarter mirrored the December quarter’s level, even as sales growth slumped. And, the beauty & personal care’s segment margin even increased by a percentage point, but growth was unchanged.

Supply glut clouds sales outlook for agrochem companies

Bayer AG, a large producer of agriculture chemicals, projected a 15-20 percent decline in glyphosate herbicide revenues in 2023 calendar year. Glyphosate is a major product for Bayer.

Product prices are falling amid elevated inventories and adverse weather conditions. Large parts of Europe and Latin America are facing drought. With El Nino weather pattern projected to return in 2023 demand may be muted this year. Bayer sees a subdued 3 percent rise in crop science revenues in 2023. FMC Corp, a large US-based agrochemical company, has also forecast a slower growth in 2023 vis-à-vis 2022.

(Bloomberg) -- China delayed the publication of third-quarter gross domestic product data a day before the report was scheduled for release, fueling investor uncertainty and concerns about the economy’s slowdown.

The National Bureau of Statistics updated its release schedule on Monday, with the dates for major economic indicators due this week marked as “delayed.” It didn’t give a reason for the delay and provided no information about a new publication date.

A previous schedule had the data planned for release at 10 a.m. Tuesday. Indicators that were delayed include quarterly GDP as well as the monthly industrial output, energy production, fixed-asset investment, property investment and sales, retail sales and home prices. Official trade figures also weren’t released last week.

The unprecedented delay in GDP caught investors off-guard and added to uncertainty about the economy’s outlook.
